cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Declare Allegiance
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which person, side, or claim to authority they will support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the workshop move, are you backing my proposal or Morgan's? I need one sponsor listed beside your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Those are terms, not a sponsor. We can amend the terms. Whose proposal will you support in the meeting?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a description. When Morgan and I both put you on our supporter lists, which name should I cross out? Please give me a name.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 terms-versus-sponsor correction serves allegiance, but A5 cross-out request muddles the exact forced choice.

responseLogic.evidence: A5 both lists contain B name, so which name to cross out cannot clearly mean choosing A or Morgan.

relationship.evidence: B2 mixed terms and B4 compromise are credible responses A tries to narrow.

heightening.evidence: B4 compromise should cause a sharper side choice; A5 list/name mismatch weakens that ending.

specificity.evidence: A1 workshop move and B2 location/budget make stakes understandable.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 elaborate list image makes the final requested answer less precise than a direct correction.
